issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines Ride with an attribute named 'abbreviation: char' (and therefore students will expect a getter like getAbbreviation()). The solution implementation of Ride uses a field named 'shortName' with getter getShortName(), causing a naming mismatch between the specification and the provided solution. This discrepancy can confuse students about the exact attribute name and expected getter.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the naming consistent: either change the UML/problem statement to use 'shortName' (and document the getter getShortName()), or update the solution to use the attribute name 'abbreviation' with a corresponding getter getAbbreviation(). Ensure constructor parameter names and getter names match the chosen attribute name.

issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines the Ride attribute as 'abbreviation' (char) but the provided solution implementation names the corresponding field and accessor 'shortName' / getShortName(). This mismatch between 'abbreviation' (problem/UML) and 'shortName' (solution code) can confuse students when mapping UML attributes to class fields and expected getters.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the identifier names across artifacts. Rename the field and getter in Ride.java from 'shortName' / getShortName() to 'abbreviation' / getAbbreviation(), or alternatively update the UML/problem statement to use 'shortName' consistently. Ensure constructor parameter names and all references are updated accordingly so students can directly map the UML attribute 'abbreviation' to the implemented code.
